title: hydnocarpus sumatranus
intro: Hydnocarpus sumatranus, commonly known as the Sumatran Birch-leaved or Sumatran water chestnut, is a plant species native to Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia and Malaysia. This plant is valued for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of fever, rheumatism, and inflammation, due to its therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic properties. The bioactive constituents of Hydnocarpus sumatranus include hydnocarpic acid, a water-soluble polysaccharide with immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory activities, and other compounds with antioxidant and antimicrobial properties. The plant's extracts have been traditionally used in folk medicine to alleviate symptoms of various diseases, although further scientific research is needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.
